data.details: Maze-like; overlooks the James; presidents and Confederate generals

data.label: Maison Rouge
data.details: Mireille's gallery and salon. Converted Victorian mansion. Hosts evening salons where art, politics, and supernatural business intertwine. The basement wine cellar has been... expanded.

data.label: Threshold
data.details: Asha's vintage shop on Ellwood. Specializes in "authentic" pieces from different eras. The changing room is a Hedge Door (currently unsafe — opening onto unfamiliar ground for three weeks).

data.label: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
data.details: Major cultural institution. Vera Solis works in the conservation department. Has wings that sometimes appear on floor plans but don't exist in the building.

data.label: 1708 Gallery
data.details: Independent contemporary art space. Marcus sometimes shows his Overwrite documentation here, though the pieces tend to "evolve" after installation.

data.label: Monument Avenue
data.details: Former Confederate statues created wounds in reality when they were erected, wounds that widened when they were removed. The Hedge grows thin here.

data.label: Arthur Ashe Monument
data.details: Stands in stark contrast to the Confederate legacy. Seems to anchor reality more firmly, but something watches from behind the tennis racket's strings.

data.label: The Empty Plinths
data.details: Where removed monuments stood. Reality is thin here. Late at night, shapes that might be statues cast shadows.

data.label: The Fan Historic District
data.details: Rows of Victorian houses. Many converted to apartments for VCU students. Some houses have more rooms inside than their exterior should allow.

data.label: Canterbury
data.details: Exclusive neighborhood. Old Richmond money. Where Power faction members live when they want to be close to Wild energy.

data.label: Riverfront Plaza
data.details: Modern office complex. Several law firms have offices here. The building has sub-basements that connect to the old canal system.

data.label: Federal Courthouse
data.details: Night faction has cultivated several court staff as assets. Some cases are decided before they're filed.

data.label: City Hall Annex
data.details: Where the real municipal business happens, away from the ceremonial main building.

data.label: James Center
data.details: Mixed-use towers. Corporate law, financial services, and discrete meeting spaces. Several Night faction fronts operate from here.

data.label: Canal Walk (Surface)
data.details: Tourist boardwalk with restaurants and shops. The public face conceals the true nature of what lies beneath.

data.label: The Old Canal Locks
data.details: Partially restored, partially flooded. Access points to deeper tunnel systems. Tourist tours end before the interesting parts.

data.label: Serrano's Domain
data.details: Network of tunnels beneath downtown. Originally shipping channels, now a vampire court. Heavily defended since the 'breach.' Additional sections have been sealed off and patrols increased. Serrano has ordered even more sections sealed after discovering fresh signs of intrusion near a previously secured access point.

data.label: The Flood Chambers
data.details: Deeper sections that can be rapidly flooded to prevent intrusion. Serrano's last line of defense.

data.label: The Exchange
data.details: Upscale restaurant and bar. Night faction's neutral ground for business meetings. Mortals welcome but carefully watched. The General has recently increased his presence here, making it a focal point of faction tensions. Staff have been observed deferring more openly to The General's preferences, and some regular patrons have begun taking their business elsewhere. Night-shift staff have also begun logging deliveries and messages that no known network claims, and the discrepancy is quietly noted in the venue's own records. A medium has been seen lingering near the bar, asking after a ghost more persistently, and her questions have not gone unnoticed by staff or by parties who track the monster-poaching market. She has now begun waiting through the late shift, and staff describe her presence as a standing unease; her vigil has settled into the venue's nightly rhythm, with staff quietly tracking when she arrives and leaves.

data.label: The Club at 101
data.details: Private club in the penthouse of a financial building. Members-only. The real membership list is very different from the official one.

data.label: Hibbs Hall
data.details: Philosophy department headquarters. Dr. Olave's office occupies the entire top floor, which has more space inside than the building's exterior suggests. The closed faculty meetings held here have grown more exclusive, and junior faculty and Consilium members have begun to notice who is no longer invited. A second, smaller meeting has begun convening on the same floor with a hand-picked subset of the Consilium, and the exclusion list has widened again. Overwrite-related files have begun being moved to the top floor, out of the reach of excluded members.

data.label: Cabell Library
data.details: Massive research library. Special Collections contains books that shouldn't exist. The basement levels extend deeper than official plans show.

data.label: Harris Hall
data.details: Mathematics building. Prof. Tanaka's office overlooks Monroe Park. She has whiteboards covered in equations that describe impossible geometries. *Olave's closed faculty meetings are held here.* A new whiteboard has been set up near Tanaka's desk covered in notes referencing the Maren Voss fragment, now cross-referenced against archival records pulled from Special Collections.

data.label: Fine Arts Building
data.details: Art history department has a private collection of Richmond artwork that shows different scenes depending on when you look at them.

data.label: Main Hospital
data.details: VCU Health's primary facility. Power faction uses medical access for research into life, death, and consciousness.

data.label: Medical Education Building
data.details: Where Power faction members train new mages in the intersection of magic and medicine.

data.label: Research Labs
data.details: Cutting-edge facilities that sometimes produce impossible results. The ethics review board has learned not to ask too many questions about certain projects.

data.label: The Observatory
data.details: Hidden facility built into the structure of multiple university buildings. Accessible through a network of maintenance tunnels and forgotten sub-basements. Contains the true Consilium library and ritual spaces.

data.label: Monroe Park
data.details: Central campus green space. The ley line beneath the park has run measurably off-tempo three times in six weeks. Power faction monitors this closely.

data.label: The Commons
data.details: Student center and gathering space. The Power faction monitors student population for potential Awakening candidates.

data.label: Creighton Renaissance (Phase A)
data.details: New mixed-income units where displaced families have returned. Some units overlook spaces where the old buildings still exist in parallel time.

data.label: The Courts
data.details: Remaining original buildings scheduled for demolition. Families live knowing their homes have expiration dates. Some buildings appear empty but show signs of ongoing habitation.

data.label: Transition Housing
data.details: Scattered sites where displaced families wait for new units. RRHA vouchers sometimes lead to addresses that don't exist on current maps.

data.label: East End Family Resource Center
data.details: Provides services, food pantry, and meeting space. Sister Catherine's domain. Sometimes serves families who died years ago but still need help. Pantry intake continues logging names and vouchers that don't match current RRHA records; the second, unshared ledger behind the counter has grown, and Sister Catherine's cross-check against older parish records has surfaced at least one name that appears in the parish archive but matches no living resident roll.

data.label: Oakland Cemetery
data.details: Historic African-American cemetery that borders the community. Graves sometimes show fresh flowers on plots that have been empty for decades.

data.label: Corner Stores
data.details: Neighborhood markets that serve as informal community hubs. Owners know everyone's business and notice when temporal anomalies affect their customers.

data.label: The Old Armstrong Site
data.details: Former high school being developed as mixed-income housing. Construction workers find classrooms with lessons still on the boards.

data.label: The Playground That Wasn't
data.details: Children play on equipment that doesn't appear in any development plans, but has been there "forever" according to residents.

data.label: Nine Mile Road Overpass
data.details: Where the community connects to the wider city. Graffiti sometimes appears in styles from decades past, depicting events that haven't happened yet.

data.label: The Historic District
data.details: 19th-century worker cottages on narrow lots. Some houses show room additions from multiple time periods existing simultaneously.

data.label: Student Blocks
data.details: Rental properties near VCU campus. Landlords sometimes collect rent for apartments that existed in previous configurations of the buildings.

data.label: The Old Families
data.details: Long-term residents in houses passed down through generations. These families anchor the community's memory and cultural continuity.

data.label: St. Andrew's Episcopal Church
data.details: Built with Grace Arents funding in 1894. Services sometimes include parishioners from different eras of the neighborhood's history.

data.label: William Byrd Community House
data.details: Provides social services and meeting space. Programs occasionally serve participants who died years ago but continue attending.

data.label: Arents Free Library
data.details: Small neighborhood library. Books sometimes include local histories that describe events before they happen.

data.label: Byrd Park Overlook
data.details: Scenic views of the James River where residents gather. Sometimes shows industrial landscape from the valley's manufacturing heyday.

data.label: The Art Collective
data.details: Informal spaces where local artists work and display. Exhibitions sometimes include work by artists who haven't moved to the neighborhood yet.

data.label: Home Studios
data.details: Many residents work from converted garages and basements. Musicians hear echoes of industrial rhythms in their compositions.

data.label: Hollywood Cemetery Border
data.details: The neighborhood's western edge where residents walk among Civil War graves and famous burials. New graves occasionally appear for living residents.

data.label: Tredegar Overlook
data.details: Views of the old iron works site below. Workers sometimes appear at the historical park, continuing shifts that ended 150 years ago.

data.label: The Expressway Cut
data.details: Where the Downtown Expressway carved through the neighborhood in the 1970s. The road sometimes shows different routes or doesn't exist at all.

data.label: The Nail
data.details: A corner bar in Oregon Hill. Corner booth against the wall, no window, furthest from the door. TV behind the bar.

data.label: Cutler's Gym
data.details: The burned-down remains of Cutler's Gym on Decatur Street; an affected anchor for Jacob Boone and Cristoff LePierre.

data.label: Virginia War Memorial
data.details: A long wall of names on Gambles Hill above the river, with a shrine at its foot where visitors leave flowers and unit patches.

data.label: Gambles Hill
data.subtype: Bluff / state offices and old mansions
data.details: A bluff of state offices, quiet law firms and old mansions where Power brokers meet "by accident" over the river view.

data.label: Tredegar Edge
data.details: A riverside lot below the bluff where the old ironworks meets the memorial grounds, ringed with rusted rail and cast-iron scrap.

data.label: Richmond Marine Terminal
data.details: The deepwater port on Deepwater Terminal Road: cranes, stacked containers and the barge berths where river freight comes ashore.

data.label: Rocketts Landing
data.details: The old port across the water on the north bank: the Intermediate Terminal, restored warehouses and a long river walk where the city first took ships.

data.label: Belle Isle
data.details: A rocky island in the middle of the James, a Civil War prison site now crossed by footbridges, climbers and fishing lines.

data.label: Manchester Floodwall
data.details: The concrete floodwall and old docks of Manchester on the south bank, where the Slave Trail begins its walk up to the city.

data.label: Mayo Bridge (south end)
data.details: The south landing of the Mayo Bridge, where the road meets the Manchester shore under the railway trestles and the floodwall.

data.label: Commerce Road Yards
data.details: A corridor of rail sidings, cold storage and blank warehouses behind the terminal, locked by day and loud by night.

data.label: Warwick Beneath
data.details: The burned colonial port town of Warwick, torched in 1781, lying under the terminal. On certain tides its streets, wharves and chimneys can be walked.

data.label: The Viaduct Camp
data.details: Tents, pallet porches and a shared kitchen tarp tucked under the I-95 viaduct, run by house rules the residents wrote themselves: quiet hours, a tool library, a rotating night watch, and a rule that nobody gets moved along without a vote.

data.label: Valley Courts Annex
data.details: A fictional courthouse annex: a security line, a clerk's counter, hard benches and a hallway where the day's docket decides whether a family keeps a car or a job.

data.label: Valley Resource Center
data.details: A fictional intake office on Lamplighter Way offering ID help, mail, showers, a computer bank and a caseworker line that moves on its own time. It stands in for the real service providers of the area, none of which appear in play.

data.label: The Night Wing
data.details: A fictional night wing of a fictional regional jail, reached by a sally port off Lamplighter Way. Lights stay half up, and everyone inside is somebody's brother, mother or coworker waiting on a hearing.

data.label: Richmond Highway Motel Strip
data.details: A fictional cluster of extended-stay motels along the Richmond Highway (US-1) corridor south of the river: weekly rates, hot plates, kids on bikes in the lots and a laundromat that never closes. A corridor, not a neighborhood.

data.label: The Red Lantern Motor Inn
data.details: A faded motor inn whose lounge has outlasted three owners. A red paper lantern over the door, a jukebox that still takes quarters, and a payphone in the lot where something fae is said to be trapped.

data.label: The Collector
data.details: An entity that catalogs things-that-remember — living artifacts, creatures with memory, and supernatural witnesses. Killed graduate student Maren Voss eight months ago. Still active in the city. The specimen in the Shockoe Bottom warehouse was hiding from it, and it may have noticed the warehouse activity.
data.next_pressure: Choose a known witness or memory-bearing object connected to the warehouse and establish how to protect it.

data.label: The Fae-Adjacent Specimen
data.details: The fae-adjacent specimen's five-day retrieval deadline (from 2026-04-24) has passed. It remains in the warehouse, but the situation is more urgent. Petra Holt's principals have now moved to direct action, sending an associate to the warehouse vicinity. The associate left a marked envelope at the warehouse entrance, indicating an imminent approach. Continuity repair: Cristoff retrieved the marked envelope. The separately reported box containing a demon heart was taken by a cleanup crew after the gym fire; no link to the fae-adjacent specimen is established.
data.next_pressure: Use the retrieved envelope to decide whether to contact Petra, protect the warehouse, or challenge the retrieval demand.

data.label: Maren Voss's Ritual Circle
data.details: Maren Voss was one of three practitioners who ran a folk-practice ritual in the warehouse. The other two are unnamed and unwarned. They do not know what they started. Maren's dying message: keep them out of it if you can. A student researcher at Cabell Library uncovered a fragment of Maren's field notes, drawing renewed academic interest in her work. Prof. Tanaka has independently confirmed a mathematical pattern in the fragment suggesting a third participant, and has begun quietly cross-referencing University archival records to try to identify them — moving the circle closer to institutional attention without yet naming anyone.
data.next_pressure: Follow the Cabell Library field-note fragment, approach Prof. Tanaka about the pattern, or compare the warehouse evidence.

data.label: Petra Holt & Unnamed Principals
data.details: Petra Holt arrived at Gild coffee shop with institutional backing and a six-day retrieval deadline for the specimen. She knows enough to use the word 'containment' correctly. Her unnamed principals are connected to a rival Power faction. If the deadline passes, they become an active problem. The deadline has passed; the associate retrieved the marked envelope and reported back. Direct action is imminent.
data.next_pressure: Approach Petra about the expired demand and the marked envelope.

data.label: Consilium Politics & the Engineered Awakening Program
data.details: Dr. Olave holds closed Consilium meetings that exclude some Power faction members — the hierarchy is shifting, and the exclusion list has widened again, deepening the internal fracture; a smaller, hand-picked meeting now convenes alongside the larger one, and Overwrite-related files are being quietly reassigned away from excluded members. Simultaneously, Councilor Marcus Voss runs a secretive program to engineer Awakenings in promising VCU students. Councilor Ingrid Voss is hiding the fact that her own Awakening was engineered decades ago by something she has never fully identified, and her quiet checks have now reached restricted University archival material — she has requested a second, narrower set of restricted records and been seen leaving with unlogged copies.
data.next_pressure: Approach an excluded faculty member or investigate the reassignment of Overwrite files.

data.label: The Compromised Hunter Network
data.details: Someone senior inside a Richmond hunter network accessed an operative's father's operational files and weaponized them to send the operative to kill a protected woman. A parallel inside-investigation is underway. The handler failed to produce the agreed password on the night of the warehouse op — compromised or impostor. A sealed field-research case from the elder Voss may contain the traitor's name.
data.next_pressure: Pursue the failed password, the sealed research case, or an established hunter contact.

data.label: The Tobacco Warehouse Operation
data.details: A tobacco warehouse on the Canal Walk edge of Shockoe Bottom was flagged by the hunter network under suspicious circumstances. Dr. Linh Pham fled it before being intercepted. Whatever was happening inside was not finished when the operative withdrew. It overlaps with the Overwrite activity and the fae specimen site. The Overwrite has begun rewriting the warehouse's administrative records, making its history unstable and drawing renewed attention from Petra Holt's principals.
data.next_pressure: Compare a surviving warehouse record with the site or seek Linh Pham’s account.

data.label: The Unknown Text Sender
data.details: An unknown third party texted an operative their own name and warned them they were watching the wrong door on the night of the warehouse op. They have not been responded to. Identity unknown. They know the operative's name and operational position. A second, unlogged contact surfaced through ordinary institutional channels in Downtown and Shockoe Bottom, indicating the sender is tracking established routines rather than only the original night. The pattern has now extended into the night-shift routines of Downtown venues and the Canal Walk, where unlogged messages and deliveries continue to appear without any known network claiming them, and night-shift staff have begun quietly comparing notes. Still unidentified and unresponded to.
data.next_pressure: Respond to the original contact or compare the unlogged messages with night-shift staff.

data.label: The Ghost of a Dead Vampire
data.details: A current mark on the monster-poaching market — the ghost of a dead vampire, something that shouldn't exist twice. Whatever it leaves behind is worth money. Not yet engaged. A nameless ghost in the same hub has been mistaken for it once already. A mortal medium who can see the nameless ghost has begun quietly asking after its story among Downtown night contacts, and word of her questions has reached parties who track the poaching market. Those parties have now moved from rumor to quiet confirmation of the mark's presence in Downtown, positioning the mark and the mistaken identity nearer to each other without naming either or making contact.
data.next_pressure: Investigate the mark through an established Downtown contact or check the medium’s account.

data.label: The General's Coup
data.details: A wolf holds damaging information on a vampire faction leader (The General) and is using it to manipulate them with coup bait. The General is volatile. If they call the bluff or move first, the wolf is in serious danger. The General has recently made a public show of force at The Exchange, consolidating control and escalating tensions. He has now begun tightening his grip on Downtown night venues, making his move unmistakable.
data.next_pressure: Choose whether to negotiate with the General, test the leverage, or withdraw from the standoff.

data.label: The Breach in Serrano's Domain
data.details: Something came through a sealed access point in Aldric Serrano's tunnel domain beneath Downtown. He has been defensive and secretive, sealing off entire sections of the canal tunnels. The nature of what breached is unknown. Serrano has discovered fresh signs of intrusion near a previously sealed access point, prompting him to further seal sections and increase patrols.
data.next_pressure: Seek Serrano’s terms for access or compare the security guard’s observations with the known breach.

data.label: The Overwrite
data.details: A city-wide supernatural phenomenon rewriting physical and historical reality across all of Richmond's hubs. Shockoe Bottom: buildings appear/disappear, street signs shift. Downtown: legal records rewrite themselves. Creighton Court: temporal displacement, different eras coexist. The University: impossible research results, contradictory academic records. Oregon Hill: industrial echoes, phantom work shifts.
data.next_pressure: Choose one already recorded discrepancy and a way to preserve or compare it.

data.label: Creighton Court Redevelopment & Temporal Displacement
data.details: RRHA's Renaissance redevelopment is displacing East End families while the Overwrite's temporal displacement anomaly makes different eras of Creighton Court coexist simultaneously. Demolished buildings cast shadows, children play on removed equipment, residents encounter neighbors who died or moved away years ago. The displacement has now begun reaching the neighborhood's ordinary institutional routines: the East End Family Resource Center's pantry intake is logging names and vouchers that don't match current RRHA records, and Sister Catherine Burke has started keeping a separate, unshared ledger for them. Her cross-check of the anomalous entries against older parish records has now surfaced a name that appears in the parish archive but matches no living resident roll, making the discrepancy harder to dismiss as clerical error.
data.next_pressure: Ask Sister Catherine for permission to compare an anomalous voucher, its parish record, and the current resident roll.

data.label: A Nameless Ghost — Identity & Anchor
data.details: A nameless ghost has no memory of life. An anchor place pulls at him somewhere in Downtown — he hasn't found it. The Overwrite's administrative anomaly in Downtown shifts identities and records, creating a particular danger for a ghost with no name. Vera (NPC medium) can see him clearly and is waiting for something he doesn't know he has. Her quiet inquiries have grown more persistent, and she has begun lingering near The Exchange and other Downtown night venues, asking after the ghost's story more openly. Her questions have drawn the attention of parties who track the monster-poaching market, who are quietly confirming the standing mark's rumored presence in Downtown — bringing the medium and the mistaken identity closer together without contact. She has now begun waiting through the late shift at The Exchange and leaving offerings at a second Downtown location; her vigil has become a fixture of the venue's late hours, deepening the pressure without any contact or confirmation of a link.
data.next_pressure: Meet the medium during her established vigil at The Exchange, observe from a distance, or investigate the anchor through Downtown records.
